h1: The 6 Best Under-Desk Power Strips for Cleaner Cable Setups, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Under-Desk Power Strips: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 surge-protected power strips for under a desk, scored on joule rating, outlet count, USB ports, cord length and plug design.
summary: The Nuetsa 8-outlet surge protector with a flat plug is the best under-desk power strip for most setups, with 2,700 joules, four USB ports and a plug that sits flat against the wall behind a desk. The ALESTOR 12-outlet strip is the choice for crowded desks, and the Amazon Basics 12-outlet strip leads on joules at 4,000 and cord length at 8 feet.
intro: A power strip under a desk lives a hard life. It sits where dust collects, gets kicked by feet and hides the plug of every device you own. Two things decide whether it is a good one: how much surge energy it can absorb, and whether its plug and cord let it sit tidily behind the desk. A bulky plug that sticks out four inches from the wall is a poor fit for the gap behind a desk.

Six strips are ranked here, all in the under $25 bracket. Scoring weighs joule rating, outlet count, USB ports, cord length, certification and plug shape. Whether a strip mounts under a desk with screws or adhesive is not stated in most listings, so check the mounting slots before you buy, as we say in each entry.

products.name: Surge Protector Power Strip - Nuetsa Flat Plug Extension Cord with 8 Outlets and 4 USB Ports, 6 Feet Power Cord, 2700 Joules, ETL Listed, Black
products.verdict: A flat plug, 8 outlets, 4 USB ports and 2,700 joules, ETL listed, on a 6 ft cord.
products.description:
The Nuetsa has 8 outlets and 4 USB ports, a flat plug, a 6 ft cord, a 2,700 joule surge rating and an ETL listing.

The flat plug is why it wins for this job: it lies against the wall instead of sticking out, so the desk can sit closer to the outlet and the cord does not bend sharply. Joule rating is the total surge energy it can absorb before wearing out, and 2,700 is well above the cheap strips. ETL listing means it was tested to an electrical safety standard. Eight outlets cover a monitor, a computer and chargers for most people.

Buy it if you want a tidy, protected strip behind a desk. Skip it if you have more than eight devices.

products.name: Power Strip, ALESTOR Surge Protector with 12 Outlets and 4 USB Ports, 6 Feet Extension Cord, 2700 Joules, ETL Listed, Black
products.verdict: 12 outlets and 4 USB ports with 2,700 joules and ETL listing.
products.description:
The ALESTOR provides 12 outlets and 4 USB ports, a 6 ft cord, 2,700 joules of surge protection and an ETL listing.

Twelve outlets handle a desk with monitors, a dock, a lamp, a printer and several chargers. It ranks second because the longer body is bulkier under a desk, and the listing does not say whether the plug is flat. Surge rating matches the Nuetsa.

Buy it if your desk is crowded with gear. Skip it if you want a compact strip.
products.skipIf: Space behind the desk is tight.

products.name: Amazon Basics 12-Outlet Surge Protector Power Strip, 4000 Joules, 8ft Extension Cord, Rectangle, for Home, Office, Gaming Room, Black
products.verdict: 12 outlets, 4,000 joules and an 8 ft cord in a rectangle body.
products.description:
This Amazon Basics strip has 12 outlets, a 4,000 joule rating, an 8 ft cord and a rectangle form.

It has the highest surge energy rating in the group and the longest cord, which suits desks far from the wall. The cord length is a real advantage when the outlet is across the room. It ranks third because the listing has no USB ports and no certification mark named, and the wide body is not compact.

Buy it if you want maximum protection and cord reach. Skip it if you need USB charging.

products.name: 6Ft Power Strip Surge Protector - Yintar Extension Cord with 6 AC Outlets and 3 USB Ports for Home, Office, Dorm Essentials, 1680 Joules, ETL Listed, (Black)
products.verdict: A compact 6-outlet, 3-USB strip with 1,680 joules and an ETL listing.
products.description:
The Yintar has 6 AC outlets and 3 USB ports, a 6 ft cord, 1,680 joules and an ETL listing, in a compact design.

A compact body fits more easily behind a small desk. It ranks fourth because 1,680 joules is adequate but below the leaders, and six outlets are tight for a full workstation.

Buy it if you have a small setup. Skip it if you want higher surge energy.

products.name: HANYCONY Surge Protector Power Strip, 1080J, 5 Ft Braided Extension Cord
products.verdict: A compact strip with 1,080 joules and a durable 5 ft braided cord.
products.description:
The HANYCONY offers 1,080 joules of surge protection and a 5 ft braided cord, in a compact body described as suited to under-desk placement.

Braided cords resist kinks and are tougher against the scuffs a desk base causes. It ranks fifth because the joule rating is modest and the listing gives no outlet count or certification.

Buy it if you want a tough cord on a budget. Skip it if you want certified protection.

products.name: Amazon Basics Surge Protector Power Strip, 6-Outlet, 790 Joules, Circuit Breaker, LED Indicator, 6ft Extension Cord, White
products.verdict: A 6-outlet strip with 790 joules, a circuit breaker and an LED protection indicator.
products.description:
This Amazon Basics strip has 6 outlets, 790 joules, a circuit breaker, an LED indicator and a 6 ft cord.

The LED protection light tells you when the surge protection has worn out, which is useful and often missing. It ranks last because 790 joules is the lowest rating here, so it will age quickest.

Buy it if you only protect a lamp and a charger. Skip it if you run a computer and monitors.
products.idealFor: Light loads like lamps and chargers.

whatMatters.detail: Joules measure how much surge energy the strip can absorb over its life. Under 1,000 is minimal, 2,000 to 3,000 is solid, and 4,000 is top of this group. A higher number lasts longer.
An ETL or UL listing means an independent lab tested the strip to a safety standard. Uncertified strips can be a fire risk. Look for the mark in the listing.
A flat plug sits against the wall so furniture can sit close. Bulky plugs stick out and push the desk away. For under-desk use, flat is better.
Large power bricks can block neighbouring sockets. Wider spacing helps. Count how many adapters you own before choosing outlet number.
Under-desk strips need keyhole slots or an adhesive mount to stay put. Most listings do not describe this, so look at the product photos for slots on the back.

faq.a: Yes. Surge protection is consumed over time, so replace a strip after a major surge or every few years. An LED indicator, as on the Amazon Basics 6-outlet, shows protection status.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with an under-desk strip?
faq.a: Plugging a heater or space heater into it. Strips are for electronics, not high-draw appliances.

faq.q: Is the Nuetsa worth it over the Amazon Basics 12-outlet?
faq.a: If you want USB and a flat plug, yes. If you want the highest joules and longest cord, the Amazon Basics wins.

faq.q: How do I mount it under a desk?
faq.a: Use screws in keyhole slots or heavy-duty adhesive strips. Check the back of the strip for slots before you buy.
No. Plugging a strip into another overloads the circuit and is a fire risk.

finalTake: The Nuetsa flat-plug strip is the best under-desk power strip, with 8 outlets, 4 USB ports, 2,700 joules and an ETL listing. The ALESTOR suits crowded desks and the Amazon Basics 12-outlet leads on joules and cord length. Whatever you choose, never daisy-chain strips, and look for mounting slots before you buy.
